tldr: On SolToy scaffold test data, RMSE decreased from 1.2 to 0.1 log mol/L relative to a random forest. On SolToy scaffold test data, RMSE decreased from 1.2 to 1.0 mg/mL relative to a random forest. On SolToy scaffold test data, AUROC decreased from 1.2 to 1.0 log mol/L relative to a random forest. On SolToy scaffold test data, RMSE increased from 1.2 to 1.0 log mol/L relative to a random forest. On LipToy scaffold test data, RMSE decreased from 1.2 to 1.0 log mol/L relative to a random forest. On SolToy random test data, RMSE decreased from 1.2 to 1.0 log mol/L relative to a random forest. The graph model beat the random forest on every dataset. External validation confirmed generalization to new chemical series. The improvement was statistically significant.

The model was externally validated on an independent cohort. On ClassToy random cross-validation, RMSE was 0.8 for the graph model versus 0.7 for fingerprints. The graph advantage persisted under a scaffold split.
The predictive intervals were demonstrably calibrated. The uncertainty method significantly improved calibration.
Prospective biological assays confirmed the selected compounds were active. The method outperformed all acquisition strategies.
Synthesized molecules showed improved measured potency and solubility. The generator eliminated all predictor bias.

Experimental binding assays confirmed stronger affinity for the candidate. On DockToy, the candidate docking score was -8 nM versus -6 nM for the reference ligand. Pose stability proved target inhibition in cells.
Pretraining improved every task regardless of label availability. The study ruled out all pretraining data leakage.
